agenda_briefs.title: Council to vote on Vancouver Villages Plan and rezoning proposal
agenda_briefs.summary: Council has adopted the Villages Plan and enacted amendments to the Vancouver Official Development Plan and Zoning and Development By-law. The changes, approved on July 28, 2026, will come into force on October 27, 2026. The Villages Plan provides land use policies, heights, and densities for village areas city-wide, and repeals the RM-12 Guidelines (effective Oct 27, 2026) and the Villages Interim Rezoning Policy (effective immediately). Amendments also apply to several area plans and policies including Norquay Village, Grandview-Woodland, Marpole, Cambie Corridor, Rupert and Renfrew Station Area plans, and policies on hotel development, secured rental, seniors housing, and transit-oriented areas.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Review the adopted Villages Plan and amended policies to understand new development rules for your village-area property before the October 27, 2026 effective date.

agenda_briefs.title: Proposed: New framework for development contributions (2027–2036)
agenda_briefs.summary: Council has approved a new Amenity Cost Charge (ACC) By-Law and adopted amendments to several development contribution policies, effective September 30, 2026. Key changes include new exemptions from Community Amenity Contributions (CACs) for certain rezoning applications submitted after that date, including: 100% non-strata commercial/industrial/institutional developments under 30,000 sq ft in the South Vancouver Industrial Area; strata residential of 5 storeys or less; rental residential of 12 storeys or less (east side) or 6 storeys or less (west side); and rental residential with 20% below-market units. The Public Art Policy now only applies to rezonings submitted before September 30, 2026.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Review the new CAC exemption criteria and ACC By-Law to determine how your development projects are affected starting September 30, 2026.

agenda_briefs.title: Proposed: Council to vote on amended Heather Lands design guidelines
agenda_briefs.summary: Vancouver City Council has adopted the amended Heather Lands Special Design District Guidelines, effective July 28, 2026. The guidelines set detailed rules for buildings, public spaces, streets, landscaping, sustainability, and cultural interpretation on the Heather Lands site (4911-5255 Heather Street, 637-657 West 37th Avenue, and 620-689 West 35th Avenue). They apply to all future construction and renovations within the CD-1 North and CD-1 South zones and must be used alongside the CD-1 By-law and city-wide design guidelines.

agenda_briefs.title: Proposed: Vancouver to amend Building By-law for DCL and ACC deferrals
agenda_briefs.summary: Council will consider a bylaw amendment that would allow developers to defer payment of Development Cost Levies (DCLs) and Amenity Cost Charges (ACCs). DCLs are fees charged to new developments to help pay for community infrastructure like parks and sewers. ACCs are charges for community amenities such as daycares and libraries. If approved, the change would let builders postpone these payments, which could affect project financing and timelines for construction in Vancouver.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Watch for the council decision — this could affect your project's payment schedule if you are a developer or builder in Vancouver.

Retail expansion areas affect fewer than 4% of lots; 96% of lots allow only housing. The ODP is also amended to clarify that a development subject to two or more GLU designations is consistent if any inconsistency is minor and publicly consulted.
